Two side-by-side graphs. The left graph shows the Industry with downward sloping Demand (D) and upward sloping Supply (S) intersecting at price P1. A horizontal dotted line extends from P1 to the right graph. The right graph shows a single Firm with a horizontal demand curve labelled D = P = AR = MR at price P1. The Y-axes are Price/Cost, X-axes are Quantity. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

Long-run equilibrium of a firm under monopolistic competition. Downward sloping AR and MR curves. A U-shaped LAC curve is exactly tangent to the downward-sloping AR curve at the equilibrium price and quantity. LMC cuts MR exactly below the tangency point. No shaded profit area (normal profit only). Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

A graph showing the Short-Run Average Total Cost (ATC), Average Variable Cost (AVC), and Marginal Cost (MC) curves. The MC curve cuts through the lowest points of both AVC and ATC. A horizontal line drawn at the minimum of ATC is. A horizontal line drawn at the minimum of AVC is. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

A graph showing the long-run equilibrium of a perfectly competitive firm. A horizontal P=AR=MR line. A U-shaped Long-Run Average Cost (LAC) curve rests its lowest point exactly on the AR line. A Long-Run Marginal Cost (LMC) curve cuts through this lowest tangent point from below. Point of intersection is the long-run equilibrium point. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

Monopoly equilibrium graph. Downward sloping AR and MR curves (MR is steeper and below AR). A U-shaped MC curve cuts MR from below at quantity Q. A vertical line goes up from Q to the AR curve to determine price P. An ATC curve sits below the price point. A shaded rectangle indicates supernormal profit. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.
